text:
Detroit's season is being played around an empty chair. Dylan Larkin asked for a trade in the summer, then refused to play until he gets one, and the Red Wings suspended him without pay at the end of October. The headlines now are about trade lists (one report says he believes ten teams is enough) and pitches for who could replace him. The club says it won't name a captain this season. Moritz Seider has become the voice of the room, and lately that voice sounds frustrated.

The frustrating part is that the hockey underneath isn't bad. The Wings get 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and have scored almost 12 fewer goals than those chances deserved, the worst finishing luck in this group. Our numbers say they deserved about 21 points; they have 17. The line of Alex DeBrincat, Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard has outscored teams 8-1.

But the last week has been genuinely poor: four straight losses, outscored 13-5, with only 43% of the chances. John Gibson has stopped .856 over his last five starts after an injury scare that brought Michal Postava up and back down. Seider and Ben Chiarot, the top pair, are minus five.

At 7-9-3 the playoff odds sit at 20%. What to watch is less a line combination than a phone call: every week Larkin sits makes this season harder to save.
headline: The Red Wings without their captain
